title: Transfer of Fourier concentration
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f,g:\\{−1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$, and let $\\mathcal F$ be any family of subsets of the $n$ coordinates. If the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of $f$ over sets outside $\\mathcal F$ is at most $\\varepsilon_1$, and the square of the uniform $L^2$ norm of $f-g$ is at most $\\varepsilon_2$, then the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of $g$ over sets outside $\\mathcal F$ is at most $2(\\varepsilon_1+\\varepsilon_2)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f,g$ are real-valued functions on the sign cube
$\\mathcal F$ is a family of coordinate subsets
the Fourier weight of $f$ outside $\\mathcal F$ is at most $\\varepsilon_1$
the square of the uniform $L^2$ norm of $f-g$ is at most $\\varepsilon_2$
